question.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\}$ is a partition of the interval $[1,3]$

- ${P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is a partition of the interval $[3,6]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we can write the summation as

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ and ${\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}$ are just the lengths of the intervals $[1,3]$ and $[3,6]$ respectively. So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =3-1=2, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =6-3=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining our results, we have

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}=2\cdot 3=6.
$$
